chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who designates something for his children while they are young, then it occurs to him to include others from his children with them, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.يَبْدُو لَهُ: it occurs to him/seems fit to him

ai.seo_question: Can a father change his mind and include other children in a gift designated for his young children?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits a father to alter his initial endowment (*hibah*) for young children by including other offspring, reflecting the Shia juristic view that such gifts remain revocable or modifiable until possession is fully established. This ruling underscores the flexibility in family wealth distribution, allowing parents to adjust provisions based on changing circumstances or equity among heirs, provided the children are still minors and the gift has not been irrevocably sealed. The permissibility highlights the distinction between a mere promise and a completed transfer of ownership in Islamic inheritance law.
